children: Malaysia's consumer inflation likely rose 2.0% on year in September, gaining slightly from 1.9% in August, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. The slight increase likely reflects higher unsubsidized fuel costs, partly offset by softer food prices and renewed electricity relief measures, says ANZ economist Sanjay Mathur in a note. Core inflation is estimated to have remained broadly stable at 1.7%, as domestic demand remains too weak to generate significant price pressures, he says. Despite the benign inflation outlook, Bank Negara Malaysia is expected to raise its policy rate by 25 bps next month as part of policy normalization, he adds. The CPI data for September are due later Monday. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
